summary: Japan has launched its historic Martian Moons eXploration (MMX) sample-return mission, aiming to gather soil from Mars' moon Phobos and return it to Earth. In civil space developments, NASA’s simulated Mars crew has completed one year inside their isolation habitat, while the Curiosity rover continues monitoring clouds in the Martian atmosphere. National security space operations saw heightened tension as a Russian satellite performed potentially dangerous maneuvers near an ICEYE spacecraft, coinciding with announcements that Space Forces Central expects a fivefold growth in coming years and that EraDrive secured a $13 million Department of Defense contract for an autonomy module. In the commercial sector, UARX Space is troubleshooting technical anomalies encountered during the maiden flight of its Orbital Transfer Vehicle, and flight-software startup WarpWare successfully closed a pre-seed funding round. Recent astronomical findings include the James Webb Space Telescope's detection of metal-rich gas surrounding the Milky Way's central black hole, the Euclid space telescope's discovery of its first comet 810 million miles from Earth, and new lunar analysis showing 10,000 surface cracks formed by the shrinking moon. Looking ahead, scientists are urging the international community to hold an ethical debate before any future Mars terraforming efforts begin.
